Multiple Sensor Positioning for Mattress type Infant Heartbeat and 
Respiration Monitoring System 
 
Sooji Park1, Hwajin Choi1, Yun La Yang1, Soo Kyeong Han1, Min-A Kim1 and Hangsik Shin1 1Department of Biomedical Engineering, Chonnam National University, Yeosu, Republic of Korea 
E-mail: hangsik.shin@jnu.ac.kr 
Abstract— The purpose of this research is to find 
the optimal sensor attachment position in mattress 
type infant monitoring system. For this, we 
analyzed the relationship between infant size and 
sensor placement, and validate the suitability of 
proposed concept using mass phantom. We tested 
the sensor placement with 5 different infant 
positions, and confirm that at least one or more 
sensors are properly located on the site of cardiac 
and respiratory activity measurement. 
Keywords— Force Sensing Resistor, Sudden Infant 
Death Syndrome, Unconstrained Monitoring 
I. INTRODUCTION 
SIDS (Sudden Infant Death Syndrome) is the leading 
cause of infant death. SIDS is the unexpected death of 
infants less than a year old, and the exact mechanism of 
SIDS is still unknown [1]. Most of the SIDS occurs 
during sleep. Center for disease control reports that 
about 2,000 infants have died from a SIDS and it is 
about half of total infant death [2]. To prevent SIDS, 
continuous monitoring of the infant is very important. 
Especially, cardiac and respiratory activity is the most 
important index for decision on infant condition. In this 
research, we researched the optimal sensor position to 
develop an unconstrained infant monitoring system. We 
developed the sensing platform using force sensor and 
fabricated it according to the standard infant body size. 
II. METHODS 
We implemented mattress-type monitoring platform 
using multiple force sensors. Totally, four piezo -
resistive force sensing resistors, FSR-408 (Interlink 
Electronic, Camarillo, USA) is attached in parallel on 
the memory-foam mattress (Kizco, Incheon, Korea) to 
measure the signal from infant. Mattress size is 87 cm × 
56.5 cm × 3 cm (height × width × depth) and it is 
enough to use for an infant less than 1 years old. 
Sensors are located on the mattress according to the 
standard infant’s body size. Generally, it is known that 
the height of newborn and 12-month infant is about 49 
cm and 75 cm, respectively [3]. In case of infants, one-
fourth of height is head length, so we divide the total 
infant height by 4 sections and determine the second 
section and one-fourth of the third section as an activity 
region to include the chest and upper part of the 
stomach. Finally, sensors are located horizontally in 
every 12.3 cm. Dimensions and sensor locations are 
described in Fig. 1. 
 
Fig. 1. Sensor placement for a mattress type infant heartbeat 
and respiration monitoring 
III. RESULTS 
We made mass phantom of infant and validated the 
suitability of sensor placement. Phantom is designed to 
have a similar size (52.5 cm) and weight (4.26 kg) 
compared with actual infant. Sensor placement was 
tested by 5 different phantom locations; upper straight, 
upper oblique (left, right), middle straight and lower 
straight. In every case, we confirmed that at least one or 
more sensor recognize the presence of phantom. 
IV. CONCLUSION 
This is the preliminary study of mattress type non -
constrained infant monitoring system. Our future work 
is to develop the system, including the heart rate and 
respiration detection algorithm based on proposed 
sensing platform.
